classification.difficultyReason: Translate graph intercepts and crossing, touching or flattened-crossing behaviour into factors and multiplicities, then choose 1 or -1 from the right-tail direction.

content.prompt: The diagrams below have leading coefficients either $1$ or $-1$. Write the equation of each polynomial.

spec.description: Ungrid­ded axes with a cubic crossing at −2, 0 and 1; left tail down and right tail up. Numeric labels only at −2 and 1.
spec.mathematics: P(x)=x(x+2)(x-1). Vertical plotting units are schematic and unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is a permanent student given; its equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The curve crosses at $x=-2,0,1$, so each root is single. The right tail rises, so the leading coefficient is $1$.
$$P(x)=x(x+2)(x-1).$$

spec.description: Ungrid­ded axes; both tails rise. Crossings at −3 and 2 and a double root at the origin, approached from below. Numeric labels only at −3 and 2.
spec.mathematics: P(x)=x^2(x+3)(x-2). Vertical plotting units are schematic and unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is a permanent student given; its equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The curve crosses at $x=-3$ and $x=2$, giving single roots. It bounces at $x=0$, giving a double root. Both tails rise, so the leading coefficient is $1$.
$$P(x)=x^2(x+3)(x-2).$$

spec.description: Ungrid­ded axes; both tails rise. A single crossing at −2 and a flattened crossing at 2. Preserve the source tick at 2.
spec.mathematics: P(x)=(x+2)(x-2)^3, matching the supplied graph and the source's triple-root convention. Vertical plotting units are schematic and unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is a permanent student given; the corrected equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The curve crosses normally at $x=-2$, giving a single root. It crosses with flattening at $x=2$, giving a triple root. Both tails rise, so the leading coefficient is $1$.
$$P(x)=(x+2)(x-2)^3.$$

spec.description: Ungrid­ded axes; both tails fall. Double root at −2, touched from below, and single crossings at 0 and 1. Preserve the source tick at −2.
spec.mathematics: P(x)=-x(x-1)(x+2)^2. Vertical plotting units are schematic and unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is a permanent student given; its equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The curve bounces at $x=-2$, giving a double root, and crosses at $x=0,1$, giving single roots. Both tails fall, so the leading coefficient is $-1$.
$$P(x)=-x(x-1)(x+2)^2.$$

spec.description: Ungrid­ded axes; left tail falls and right tail rises. Flattened crossing at −1 and a bounce from above at 2. Preserve ticks at −1 and 2.
spec.mathematics: P(x)=(x-2)^2(x+1)^3. Vertical plotting units are schematic and unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is a permanent student given; its equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The curve crosses with flattening at $x=-1$, giving a triple root, and bounces at $x=2$, giving a double root. The right tail rises, so the leading coefficient is $1$.
$$P(x)=(x-2)^2(x+1)^3.$$

spec.description: Ungrid­ded axes; left tail rises and right tail falls. Flattened crossing at the origin and a bounce from below at 2. Preserve the source tick at 2.
spec.mathematics: P(x)=-x^3(x-2)^2. Vertical plotting units are schematic and unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: The graph is a permanent student given; its equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The curve crosses with flattening at $x=0$, giving a triple root, and bounces at $x=2$, giving a double root. The right tail falls, so the leading coefficient is $-1$.
$$P(x)=-x^3(x-2)^2.$$
